name: Tute individual
description: Tute for two players; no partnerships. Standard 40-card Spanish deck. Ten cards each, stock with face-up trump; follow suit and overtake; Cantes (40/20) after winning a trick; Tute (4 Kings or 4 Knights) wins the deal. Most points in the deal wins that game; session is multiple deals.

content.text: Tute for two players; no partnerships. Standard 40-card Spanish deck. Ten cards each, stock with face-up trump; follow suit and overtake; Cantes (40/20) after winning a trick; Tute (4 Kings or 4 Knights) wins the deal. Most points in the deal wins that game; session is multiple deals.
Originated in Italy (as tutti); spread to Spain in the 19th century where it became one of the most popular card games. Two-player individual variant.

Standard Spanish pack of 40 cards: four suits (Swords/espadas, Batons/bastos, Cups/copas, Coins/oros). Ranks and point values: Ace 11, Three 10, King 4, Horse 3, Jack 2; Seven through Two count zero. One suit is trump each deal, determined by the face-up card.
10 each, next card face up for trump, remainder as stock; after each trick winner draws first then others anticlockwise.
